newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia tin rises above 14 rgt, two-month high.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia tin rises above 14 rgt, two-month high.

text.p: Malaysia's spot tin price rose above the pschological level of 14 ringgit/kg, hitting a two-month high to close at 14.10 ringgit ($5.35) on increased demand, higher London and currency factors, traders said.
The metal rose 30 cents from yesterday's close.
"Sentiment was firm. There was a sudden buying here after the London market moved up last night," a trader said, adding that a weaker ringit against the U.S. dollar also underpin sentiment.
Traders said they saw an opening bid of 355 tonnes against offer of 113 tonnes.
Turnover increased to 231 tonnes from 123 on Wednesday with demand mainly from Japan, Europe and Malaysia.
"It is a firm market and buyers are cashing in to buy at current levels for fear that prices may rise," another trader said, adding that the underlying firm fundamentals also attributed to the rise.
"We are optimistic that the price may stay above 14 ringgit if London continues to rally in the near-term," he said.
The local price over London was at a $35 a tonne discount against a premium of $15 a tonne.
